scopeMarkdown:
Follow-up to the epic `gpux-virtual-list`, which must be closed before this one starts. That epic moves RayX's virtual list into gpux as `VirtualList`. It gives list layers only to vertical lists that are their own scroll container and have no sticky rows, and fixes the handle-less redraw loop, the `ParentViewport` collapse under view retention, `ParentViewport` metrics inside a div layer, and RayX's state-view rebuilds.

The owner asked (2026-10-16) for everything that epic left out:
- list layers for horizontal lists, lists with sticky rows, `SynchronizedOffset` lists and `ParentViewport` lists;
- a `ParentViewport` list's parent `div` layer that stays promoted, which means changing RayX's dependent-view invalidation;
- timings.

**Where the work lands.** It continues on the same branches in the same worktree folder (`/Users/dinko/.worktrees/virtual-list/`): gpux and RayX `feat/virtual-list`. The two pull requests (gpux into `main`, then RayX into `master`) therefore carry both epics. If the owner merges `gpux-virtual-list` first, move this epic's work to new branches by amending `repositories`.

**In scope**
- **Measured leaves under view retention (owner, 2026-10-16):** the general form of the `ParentViewport` collapse. Under layout retention, a kept view that is not built gives back measurement closures only to text leaves, so any other measured leaf whose size depends on its measurement is sized empty. A `uniform_list` with `ListSizingBehavior::Infer` and an auto height in a retained child view gives its parent a scroll extent of 0 with fast mode on, against 19,800 px with it off (recorded in `gpui/layout-style/state.md` by `gpux-virtual-list` s02). `gpux-virtual-list` fixed only `VirtualList`'s case, with a spacer.
- **Horizontal lists:** axis-generic row slots in the list layers, for `VirtualList`'s horizontal axis.
- **Sticky rows:** `VirtualList`'s sticky rows (top and left edges, levels, stack ids, push-out, `when_stuck`, `on_sticky_state_changed`) drawn above a composited layer every frame, while the layer holds the ordinary rows.
- **`SynchronizedOffset`:** a list layer driven by another container's handle.
- **`ParentViewport`:** a list inside a scrolling `div` whose layer stays promoted. The list renders rows for the layer's painted region, reads no offset there, and answers its metrics and range on composited frames. RayX stops rebuilding ListViewState and TreeState on every parent scroll.
- **RayX consumer proof** for each kind: ListView with a sticky policy, a horizontal ListView, ListView and TreeView in `ParentViewport` mode, and DataTable's synchronized rows.
- **Fast-mode bench scenarios** for every kind, with deterministic attribution counters in CI.
- **Lane G timings** on this Mac, recorded in `docs/fast-mode.md`.

**Out of scope**
- `uniform_list` and `list` with sticky items. They stay `ineligible`; the sticky overlay mechanism is built for `VirtualList`, and extending it to them is a later change.
- Timings on other platforms: lane G is macOS-only by repository decision.
- Opening the pull requests.

**Owner-attended.** The last sprint (s07) runs lane G timings on the owner's Mac with the display awake. The owner signs up for it by keeping the machine available. If it cannot run, the owner decides the timing criterion's disposition.
constraintsMarkdown:
- Keep everything `gpux-virtual-list`'s constraints say: Zed's crate boundaries, no new crate, gpux proof in gpux, frames equal to frames drawn from scratch, hooks inert with the switch off, Conventional Commits without co-author lines, paired gpux and RayX commits.
- Timings belong to lane G only. CI asserts deterministic counters, never times.
- A sticky row must keep its hitbox, listeners, semantics and DevKit identity: no proxy rows or overlay siblings detached from the row (RayX's virtualization rules).

requirements.title: Measured leaves keep their size under view retention
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A view kept without building never lays out a measured leaf as empty.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Requirement.** With view retention on, a measured leaf other than text, whose size on an axis depends on its measurement (no definite style size there), has the size its measurement gives on every frame its view is kept.

**Cases.**
- A `uniform_list` with `ListSizingBehavior::Infer` and an auto height in a retained child view, inside a scrolling `div`: the parent's scroll extent equals the fast-mode-off value on every frame, and the wheel scrolls it.
- An element built on the public `Window::request_measured_layout`, the path external custom elements use, in a retained view, as a flex child and as a scroll container's content: it keeps its measured size.
- A change of the available space while the view is kept, such as a parent resize, measures the leaf afresh.

**Equality.** Each case, for each fast-mode switch combination, shows frames equal to those of a window with fast mode off.

**Test.** A new group, `crates/gpui/tests/retained_measured_leaves.rs`. It fails on the code before the fix with a message containing `measured leaf collapsed`.

requirements.title: Half-pixel edges land alike with and without layers
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The owner asked (2026-10-16), relayed by the coordinating session: "yes, add it and fix them" — the two gaps gpux-virtual-list documented. An edge on exactly half a device pixel rounds one pixel apart in a frame shown from a scroll layer and one drawn from scratch once the layer moves it across the window's origin.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Requirement.** Frames shown from any scroll layer (a `div`'s layer, `uniform_list`, `list`, `VirtualList`) equal frames drawn from scratch, including edges that fall exactly on half a device pixel and that a layer moves across the window's origin.

**Cases.** Scale factors 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2, with paddings, row sizes and offsets that produce exact ties.

**Existing tests.** The `virtual_list_layers` groups that avoided exact ties (`changes`' whole-pixel size change, `oracle`'s scale and padding) stop avoiding them.

**Test.** A new group, `fast::tests::half_pixel_edges`, which fails on the code before the fix with a message containing `half-pixel edge`.

**Runtime proof.** Lane C's scroll-layer suites (`lane_c_scroll_layers`, `lane_c_layer_scales`) pass in full mode (`GPUX_LANE_C_FULL=1`), narrowed to those groups.

requirements.title: uniform_list keeps its measured item
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The owner asked (2026-10-16), relayed by the coordinating session: "yes, add it and fix them" — the two gaps gpux-virtual-list documented. `uniform_list` renders its first row to measure it in `request_layout` on every frame, outside `lists::measure_item`: its row closure runs once more a frame than the rows its layer renders (1.87 against 0.87 rows a frame; planning measured 1.75 against 0.75).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Requirement.** `uniform_list` keeps its measured item size while nothing the measured row read has changed.

**Scroll-only frames.** With scroll layers on, and also with view retention alone, the item closure runs only for the rows the frame renders: with layers, row closures equal `list_rows_rendered`; without layers, the rows the list shows. No frame renders the measured item again.

**Changes.** When the measured row's content or size changes, it is measured again, and frames still equal frames drawn from scratch.

**Test.** A new group, `fast::tests::uniform_measured_item`, which fails on the code before the fix with a message containing `measured again`.

**Scope.** With scroll layers on: a horizontal `VirtualList` that is its own scroll container and has no sticky rows.

**Per frame, after promotion.** On 60 horizontal wheel frames of 15 px over 10,000 variable-width columns, every scroll-only frame:
- composites (`layers_composited`);
- renders at most 2 columns on average;
- keeps the others (`list_rows_kept`).

**Placement.** The overscan runs along the x axis, and columns are placed by the list's own origins.

**Test.** A new group, `fast::tests::virtual_list_layers::horizontal`. It also replaces the horizontal case of `gpux-virtual-list`'s `ineligible` group, so a horizontal list is no longer counted `ineligible`.

**Requirement.** Frames shown from a horizontal list's layer equal frames drawn from scratch:
- quads with layers expanded, at scale factors 1 and 1.25, with fractional widths, `gap` and padding;
- whole frame descriptions over random histories of horizontal wheel turns, pointer moves, clicks and size changes.

**Test.** A new group, `fast::tests::virtual_list_layers::horizontal_oracle`.

requirements.title: Sticky virtual lists composite
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A `VirtualList` with sticky rows keeps its ordinary rows in the layer and draws its sticky rows over it every frame.

requirements.title: SynchronizedOffset virtual lists composite
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A list that applies another container's offset itself gets a list layer of its own.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Scope.** A vertical or horizontal `VirtualList` in `SynchronizedOffset` mode, driven by a scrolling container beside it (the DataTable header and body pattern).

**Required.** On scroll-only frames of the driver, the list:
- composites from its own list layer, keyed by the list;
- renders at most 2 rows on average;
- shows frames equal to frames drawn from scratch.

The notification the shared handle sends its dependent views counts as the scroll's, as for a list's own handle.

**Test.** A new group, `fast::tests::virtual_list_layers::synchronized`, with counters and a random-history oracle.

requirements.title: A ParentViewport list keeps its parent's layer
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A `ParentViewport` list inside a scrolling `div` no longer forces the div off its layer.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Required.** RayX ListView and TreeView in `ParentViewport` mode, in a scrolling `div` with fast mode on:
- keep the div's layer compositing over 60 wheel frames;
- do not rebuild their state view on scroll-only frames.

RayX's dependent-view registration on a shared external handle stays only where gpux cannot see the read itself (for example a cached view with view retention off). RayX's existing `ParentViewport` behaviour holds with fast mode on and off: programmatic `scroll_to_item`, mutation scroll preservation, follow-tail and `VisibleRangeChanged`.

**Tests.**
- A new RayX group, `crates/rayx_components/rayx_components_core/tests/parent_viewport_layers.rs`.
- RayX's existing `application_configuration_programmatic_scroll_parent_viewport` tests, selected on purpose as the preservation proof.

**CI counters.** It is listed in `fast_mode_attribution`; its deterministic counters show that `layers` composites (`tiles_composited > 0`) and renders fewer rows than `splice`, and `every_scenario_is_attributed` passes.

requirements.title: The branches carry main's AccessKit model
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The owner decided (2026-10-17), relayed by the coordinating session: "Lets skip s04 until acceskit is merged in and skip to s05 and everything that can be done until the merge". The coordinating session's plan, which the owner agreed: hold s04 until the AccessKit epic (gpux-a11y-devtools) merges into `main`; then merge `main` into `feat/virtual-list`, so that the DevKit hooks move to AccessKit there, and build s04's record hiding on the AccessKit mechanism.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Merge.** gpux `main`, with the AccessKit epic, is merged into gpux `feat/virtual-list`, and RayX `master`, with its a11y side, into RayX `feat/virtual-list`.

**Model.** `VirtualList`'s and the list layers' uses of DevKit nodes and the fast-mode scenes' `DevtoolsSemantics` move onto the AccessKit model main carries (content a layer holds off screen recorded under the window's a11y nodes; a composited layer replaying its a11y events). Main's DevKit-based record hiding is not ported.

**Proof.** This epic's and `gpux-virtual-list`'s test groups pass afterwards, in gpux and in RayX.

**Start.** Only once the owner says the AccessKit epic is merged.

requirements.title: A wheel turn over a DataTable draws the frames a scroll needs
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The owner decided (2026-10-17), relayed by the coordinating session: "Fix it" (DataTable's second frame after each wheel turn, with fast mode off too). Found by t08: a DataTable drew a second frame after every wheel turn, with fast mode off and on.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Requirement.** One wheel turn over a DataTable, across or down, draws exactly one frame, with fast mode off and with every switch on; no frame follows it once it is drawn.

**Cause.** `ScrollableMask` handled the table's wheel by queueing a programmatic offset (`request_offset`), which the header's scroll container took in at its next prepaint and published with a deferred notification, and by notifying the view itself: the deferred notification drew a second frame. It now publishes the turn as a wheel in its input turn (`ScrollHandle::publish_wheel_offset`, RayX 5b839689, gpux a4131c8).

**Test.** A new RayX group, `crates/rayx_components/rayx_components_datatable/tests/wheel_frames.rs`, naming the cause in its doc comment; it fails with the mask's old handler.
